content.en: A partnership as well as 'grantor' or 'simple' trust will have to satisfy all the following conditions:

• The partnership or trust is a direct account holder of UBS;
  • The account holder is a certified deemed-compliant FFI (other than a registered deemed-compliant Model 1 IGA FFI)1, an exempt beneficial owner, an owner-documented FFI or an NFFE (other than a Withholding partnership or trust).
  • None of the partners, beneficiaries or owners is a US person;
  • None of the partners, beneficiaries or owners are flow-through entities or acting as intermediaries; and
  • None of the partners, beneficiaries or owners is subject to FATCA withholding or reporting2.
The QI must withhold tax at the highest rate applicable to any partner, beneficiary, or owner.
In order to comply with the above conditions, the following specific QI documents are required from the partnership or trust:

• Withholding Statement and Agreement; and
  • Substitute Form W-8IMY from the partnership or trust; and
  • Official Form W-8BEN from each of the partners, beneficiaries or owners that are individuals; and/or
  • Official Form W-8BEN-E from each of the partners, beneficiaries or owners that are entities.
Please note that the above documents are kept within the bank and are not forwarded to the Internal Revenue Service.
Under the Withholding Statement and Agreement, the partnership or trust must make records available within 90 days upon request from

QI or QI's auditor. If the partnership or trust fails to comply with the request within the time limit, this might result in correction of withholding and disclosure of the partnership or trust and its partners, beneficiaries or owners to the US Internal Revenue Service.

The Substitute Form W-8IMY and agreement are in general valid without timely restriction. Other documentation such as Forms W-8BEN and/or W-8BEN-E, withholding statements, and related documentation are subject to a renewal based on applicable rules, and unless there are material changes which will require a renewal. We appreciate that the QI rules are complicated. If you are not familiar with the QI rules, please seek advice from your own legal counsels for the appropriate action that you should take.
